title: Non-soficity of OpenAI's torsion-free hyperbolic group
description: Is every word-hyperbolic group sofic? OpenAI recently constructed a torsion-free word-hyperbolic group G that is not residually finite, with a Lean formalization. We show that G is not sofic. Their rank argument against finite quotients uses a quotient only through its permutation matrices, and it survives approximation: a relation that fails on a small fraction of points costs a small rank error, and a word with few fixed points costs a small trace error. So approximate permutation models are excluded at a fixed positive accuracy, while soficity would supply them at every accuracy; moreover, one fixed nonidentity element of G dies in every sofic quotient. We formalize the conclusion in Lean on top of OpenAI's development. Sandhu and Thom independently found a different non-sofic torsion-free hyperbolic group by the same kind of rank count. The same rank count, with group elements in place of permutation matrices, excludes Linnell division rings: if K is a division ring of the characteristic q fixed by the construction and Λ is any group containing G, then K[Λ] has no Linnell division ring. In such a division ring, the defining independence conditions inside certain free subgroups of G would give the relevant matrices full rank, while OpenAI's finite-field interpolation identity forces their rank to collapse; no zero divisor is exhibited. OpenAI's torsion-free groups whose group algebras over F_2 have zero divisors, or are not directly finite, already show that Linnell division rings need not exist in characteristic two; here the group is G itself. We also show that G is the free product of a free group and a torsion-free hyperbolic group that again has no Linnell division ring in characteristic q, and we prove barriers to extending the argument to hyperlinearity. The group and every input to the non-soficity argument are OpenAI's.
